finding: Map-entry name test puts the bad entry at index 0 only, so the index fallback is not proven.
why: Every fallback case expects "map 0"; a change that returns a constant 0 or ignores path[1] in describe still passes, and no case has a non-string id.
fix: Add a case with doc["maps"] = [valid_map, "abc"] expecting "map 1", and one with {"id": 5} expecting the id name the code gives.
evidence: @pytest.mark.parametrize("entry, name", [("abc", "map 0"), (5, "map 0"), (0, "map 0"), (["x"], "map 0"), ({}, "map 0"), ({"id": "m-1"}, "map m-1")]) ; doc["maps"] = [entry]; engine.py:70 name = f"map {(entry.get('id') if isinstance(entry, dict) else None) or path[1]}" (unverified by run: read only, no mutation probe, no Java)

finding: describe() names a map by any truthy id, so a non-string id is shown as the map name instead of its index.
why: A map entry {"id": 7} fails the schema (id must be string or null) and the refusal reads "map 7, field id"; the new test covers only string ids, objects without id, and non-objects.
fix: Use entry.get('id') only when it is a non-empty str; else path[1]. Add the {"id": 7} case to test_a_bad_map_entry_is_refused_by_name.
evidence: name = f"map {(entry.get('id') if isinstance(entry, dict) else None) or path[1]}"  (unverified by run; read of page-v0.schema.json component.id type ["string","null"])

finding: Possible drifted twin: registry hard-wires page-v0.schema.json while engine.py selects the schema file by document version.
why: engine.py SCHEMA_FILES maps each schema value to its own file ("A change is a new schema value with its own file and reader"), but registry.validate always checks component shape against the v0 file, so a second schema version needs a second edit here.
fix: Pass the version's schema (or its component shape) into registry.validate from check_document, or note in a comment that components are shared across versions.
